title: The first free Summer School in Ilora
subtitle: Four weeks of learning brought 46 registered students together with nine volunteer teachers in the programme's first edition.
caption: Photographs reproduced from the 2019 first-edition report, page 6.

sections.heading: A first edition built around access
sections.text: The first Africa-RII Free Summer School took place over four intensive weeks between August and September 2019 in Ilora. The report records 46 registered students and an average daily attendance of 30 to 35. The initiative extended the organisation's earlier Train A Child Today work into a shared learning programme during the school holidays.

sections.heading: The people behind the classes
sections.text: Nine volunteer teachers supported the programme, including graduates and National Youth Service Corps members. Two support staff helped with its operation. The classroom and group photographs in the report show this first cohort and the people who worked with them.

sections.heading: Learning and everyday support
sections.text: The report records daily biscuits and sachet water for students, refreshments for volunteers, and a final examination for participating learners. These practical details formed part of the effort to make a free learning space work day by day.

sections.heading: The first year's expenditure
sections.text: Reported expenditure was NGN 300,000. The article uses the naira total printed in both the written summary and infographic. The original report is available below, including its own currency annotations; no exchange-rate conversion has been added.

title: From lockdown to a community resource centre
subtitle: The 2020 chapter follows the fundraising and rehabilitation work that created an enduring home for community learning.
caption: Resource-centre photographs from the report's 2020 development chapter, which also describes the library opening in early 2021; these are not photographs of a 2020 Summer School edition.

sections.heading: A different kind of programme year
sections.text: The report places 2020 under the COVID-19 pandemic and lockdown. Its account focuses on fundraising for the Community Resource Centre rather than recording a Summer School edition, attendance figures or a summer teaching programme.

sections.heading: Creating a permanent learning space
sections.text: The project sought to rehabilitate the former Ajayi family house in Ilora as a public community resource centre. Its objectives included a reading and book-lending library, skills and mentorship opportunities for school leavers and non-literate youths, and a safe space for children, young people and women.

sections.heading: The fundraising record
sections.text: The report describes a EUR 6,000 crowdfunding drive as the goal. It records EUR 1,679 through GoFundMe and NGN 25,000 through UBA in Nigeria, alongside a EUR 500 donation from a Dachau youth organisation and a further EUR 600 contribution from Oladapo Ajayi during the work. These amounts are kept in their original currencies; the fundraising goal is not presented as money raised.

sections.heading: From rehabilitation to daily use
sections.text: Listed work included roofing and ceiling replacement, electrical installation, structural remodelling, learning furniture, fumigation, painting, tree planting, books and commissioning. The chapter says the library had been operational since the beginning of March 2021. It describes a facility manager, cleaner, night security guard and two NYSC members supporting library, tutorial and outreach activities.

title: A second edition supported by a growing library
subtitle: The second Summer School registered 74 students, connecting holiday classes with the resource centre's wider learning support.
caption: Photographs reproduced from the 2021 second-edition report, page 10.

sections.heading: Learning beyond the holidays
sections.text: The 2021 chapter identifies this as the second edition of the Free Summer School. It describes a mutually supportive relationship between summer teaching and the Community Resource Centre's library, giving students a place to learn before and after the holiday programme.

sections.heading: The second cohort
sections.text: The report records 74 registered students, average daily attendance of 55 to 60, eleven volunteer teachers and five support staff. Registration had grown from the 46 students recorded for the first edition in 2019.

sections.heading: Classes, competitions and community outreach
sections.text: Activities included a final examination, sports and games culminating in inter-class competitions, an essay competition and an end-of-school party. The organisers also circulated flyers and raised awareness through churches and mosques in the community. Student refreshments included biscuits, soya milk and water.

sections.heading: Reading the year's figures
sections.text: The report's infographic gives a four-week programme between August and September and an expenditure total of NGN 350,000. The written duration line repeats the year 2019 beneath the 2021 heading. This article follows the edition heading and does not infer exact 2021 dates from that repeated line.

title: More learners, with practical skills alongside study
subtitle: The third edition registered 110 students and introduced a skills-acquisition series alongside the academic programme.
caption: Summer School photographs from page 12 and skills-workshop photographs from page 14 of the 2022 report.

sections.heading: The third Summer School
sections.text: The 2022 edition registered 110 students, with average daily attendance of 85 to 90. Twelve volunteer teachers and five support staff supported the programme. Its reported four-week format combined classroom learning with wider opportunities to participate and develop confidence.

sections.heading: A full programme of activities
sections.text: The report lists a final examination, an essay competition, sports and inter-class games, an end-of-programme party and local awareness work. It also records refreshments including soya milk, boiled eggs, puff-puff and water. A skills-acquisition series was introduced as part of the expanding programme.

sections.heading: The maiden skills workshop
sections.text: A separate 2022 skills-acquisition chapter describes a partnership with Professor Peju Layiwola and the Women and Youths Arts Foundation. Thirty-five students, women and young people attended training in tie-dye and resin jewellery. The report identifies a NGN 150,000 workshop budget, separate from the NGN 350,000 Summer School expenditure.

sections.heading: Source details and dates
sections.text: The skills-workshop narrative calls the programme two days, while its date range and flyer give 12–14 September 2022. The source therefore does not establish a consistent duration. The Summer School duration line also repeats 2019 beneath the 2022 heading. The figures here follow the labelled 2022 chapters; the PDF preserves the original wording for reference.

title: Academic learning, creative workshops and shared achievement
subtitle: The fourth edition registered 105 students, with 87 recorded for the final examination and a broader programme of practical activities.
caption: Photographs reproduced from the 2023 fourth-edition report, pages 16–17.

sections.heading: The fourth edition in numbers
sections.text: The 2023 report records 105 registered students and average daily attendance of 80 to 90. It records 87 under final examination, supported by twelve volunteer teachers and five support staff. The figure 87 is an examination participation count, not a pass rate or percentage.

sections.heading: Learning beyond the classroom
sections.text: Alongside academic work, the programme included an essay competition, sports and games, film day, counselling sessions, a closing party, and prize-giving and awards. Photographs document classroom groups, practical activities and presentations from this edition.

sections.heading: Practical skills and daily support
sections.text: The skills workshops covered introductory computer training, soap making, bead making and adire tie-dye. The refreshment plan included combinations of soya milk, boiled eggs, tofu, puff-puff and water. These activities extended the programme beyond lessons into creative and practical learning.

sections.heading: The expenditure record
sections.text: Both the narrative and infographic record expenditure of NGN 1,300,000. Their euro equivalents differ: the written page gives EUR 1,150, while the following infographic gives EUR 750. The article therefore reports the consistent naira total rather than selecting an unverified euro conversion. The four-week duration is taken from the edition infographic; the repeated 2019 date in the narrative is not treated as an exact 2023 date.

title: A year of pause, student support and renewal
subtitle: Summer School paused in 2024 while Africa-RII reviewed its work, supported students and maintained the Community Resource Centre.
caption: Community and student-support photographs reproduced from the 2024 chapter, page 20. Summer School was paused that year.

sections.heading: A documented pause, not a Summer School edition
sections.text: The report explicitly labels 2024 as a Free Summer School pause for evaluation, sustainability and future growth. The introductory letter describes a year of reassessment and repositioning. This article records the work that continued during that pause and does not attribute Summer School attendance or a teaching cohort to 2024.

sections.heading: Supporting the next step in education
sections.text: In February, a NGN 31,500 donation from Ms Adeoye Ariyo supported JAMB examination forms for dedicated library students. The report lists seven beneficiaries. This article presents the aggregate support rather than reproducing individual students' education and financial circumstances.

sections.heading: Maintaining the resource centre
sections.text: The September account records a EUR 500 donation, shown in the report as NGN 850,000, from a Dachau youth organisation, facilitated through Julia Wagner and Valerie Gruber. Listed works include public-toilet completion, roof repairs and a protective cage for a plant. The original currencies are retained as reported, without applying a current exchange rate.

sections.heading: Additional support and organisational renewal
sections.text: The chapter also records additional EUR 150 and EUR 200 contributions from Oladapo Ajayi for separate activities. These included small animal-rearing spaces, staff support, meetings, a NGN 25,000 emergency scholarship and governance/documentation work. The report describes a reconstituted board and plans for scholarships, digital learning, improved facilities and a return to Summer School in 2025. These are presented as the outlook recorded in the 2024 document, not as proof that every proposal was completed.

title: Learning across classrooms and communities
subtitle: The fifth edition brought 190 learners together through academic study and new creative activities.

sections.heading: The fifth edition
sections.text: Africa-RII reports that its 2025 Summer School enrolled 190 students from different villages. The fifth edition continued the organisation's free summer-learning programme, widening the opportunities available to learners during the holiday period.

sections.heading: Learning beyond textbooks
sections.text: The curriculum added graphic design, Monopoly and Ludo, film screenings and career counselling. These activities brought practical, creative and reflective experiences alongside academic study.

sections.heading: What the report records
sections.text: The organisation reports an average 87% increase in knowledge of subjects taught. This figure is presented as Africa-RII's reported result; the source does not provide a detailed assessment methodology. The photographs on this page come from the 2025 section of its Summer School archive.

title: Keeping opportunity within reach
subtitle: A journal space for the next chapter of summer learning.

sections.heading: Why keep a summer learning journal?
sections.text: An annual journal can help a community see its work over time. It gives space to the learning itself, the people who support it and the questions worth carrying into another year. This draft reserves that space for Africa-RII's 2026 Summer School story.

sections.heading: Listening as well as documenting
sections.text: A useful record includes more than a list of activities. It should explain the purpose of the learning, give context to photographs and include participants' perspectives with their permission. That approach reflects Africa-RII's wider emphasis on community-led solutions and collaboration.

sections.heading: The 2026 record
sections.text: The status, dates and activities of the 2026 edition have not been confirmed for this website. This page is neither an event announcement nor a report that the programme has taken place. The team can add a confirmed account and correctly attributed images when they are available.
